newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Brash says wants conditions in line Dec, Mar.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Brash says wants conditions in line Dec, Mar.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash told Radio New Zealand on Thursday the central bank wanted monetary conditions to be broadly in line with its assessments made in December and March.

Brash, asked in an interview what conditions the bank would want between now and the bank's monetary policy statement (MPS), said: "We want monetary conditions to be broadly in line with the announcement we made in December, confirmed in March and reaffirmed last week at select committee," Brash said.
"It doesn't mean they have to be on the line. It needs to be within cooey of that line.
"At the moment...I won't say what they are at the moment -- I haven't got a screen in front of me -- but they certainly were yesterday within cooey of that line," Brash said.

Asked earlier in the interview if the RBNZ had a "rigid line in the sand" on monetary policy, Brash said: "On the contrary, I think we allow more latitude around that line than any other central bank I'm aware of.

"Certainly, we would be happy to see conditions both firmer and easier than that line. And we don't tie down any particular interest rate or any particular exchange rate. It's the combination we are looking at.
"We are saying if it gets too far from that combination then we start getting concerned," Brash said.
The bank's monetary policy statement is due on June 27, a little later than normal.
Asked if the bank was concerned about the coalition government's first budget, Brash said: "No. We basically timed it at the end of June because we don't at this point know when the budget will be.
"It is understood to be in June. It is important I think that we have the latest fiscal information. We can't release that, clearly, before the budget does."
The New Zealand dollar closed Wednesday's trade at US$0.6930/37 and at 67.84 on the Trade-Weighted Index. Key 90-day bank bills closed at 7.02 percent.
Brash said on Wednesday the bank had received a number of critical comments after it released a statement earlier in the week saying monetary conditions had eased too far.
Conditions had eased substantially in the preceding weeks after Brash made comments in an interview which were taken by the market as a hint the bank would ease conditions in June.
Brash said that thereafter conditions eased by more than 100 basis points, expressed in interest rate terms, with a sharp fall in the exchange rate and no rise in interest rates.
"Only at that point did we indicate that conditions had moved further away from desired conditions than we felt appropriate, pending completion of our next projections," Brash said on Wednesday.
